text:
alex: Heads-up — seeing a sharp spike in outbound failures from inference pods in us-west-2 starting ~10:12 UTC. 502s/timeouts when fetching model shards and telemetry endpoints. CloudWatch for our NAT Gateway shows ActiveConnections hitting a hard plateau. Suspect ephemeral port exhaustion on the VPC egress path.

maria: Confirming. Alerts fired for NATGateway ActiveConnections and high PacketDrop. Pod logs show repeated `connect: connection reset by peer`. 

jake: Do we have a quick check of concurrent connections per source IP? NAT gateway collapses when SNAT ports run out. Can you paste `netstat` from a noisy node?

alex: Pasted from one of the nodes (truncated):
```
$ kubectl exec -n inference -it inference-pod-7 -- netstat -an | grep ESTABLISHED | wc -l
42000
$ ss -tnp | grep ESTABLISHED | head -5
ESTAB 0 0 10.0.45.12:43562 18.203.12.34:443 users:("python3",pid=1129,fd=45)
ESTAB 0 0 10.0.45.12:43563 18.203.12.34:443 users:("python3",pid=1129,fd=46)
```

alex: So ~42k established outbound sockets from a single pod/node. With NAT SNAT port pool we can hit exhaustion quickly when many pods reuse the same source IPs.

priya: That matches telemetry — our model shard downloader opened many parallel connections after the new prefetch change. We rolled that change two hours ago.

maria: Immediate mitigations we can attempt: reduce concurrency in prefetch (revert or patch), move heavy egress traffic to a dedicated egress proxy inside the VPC to multiplex connections, and add additional NAT Gateway IPs / AZ NAT gateways. Long-term: move model storage access to VPC endpoints or PrivateLink to avoid NAT entirely.

jake: For immediate triage I can: (1) patch the prefetch concurrency to 4, (2) deploy a lightweight HTTP connection pooler (squid/nginx) in the VPC and route pods through it, (3) spin up an extra NAT gateway in another AZ and add it to the route table for the egress subnets. Which order?

alex: Do 1 and 2 first — should reduce outbound concurrency fast. 3 is slower (IP/EIP allocations + route table updates) but we should do it if we see repeated spikes.

priya: I'll open a rollback PR for the prefetch change now.

sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0318-348 — NAT ephemeral ports suspected. Pager on-call if errors persist for >15m. https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-0318-348

maria: Also flagging CloudWatch metrics to watch: NATGateway.BytesOut, NATGateway.ActiveConnections, NATGateway.ConnectionAttempts. Check ELB/ALB metrics if calls are to external APIs. If ActiveConnections flatlines while rejected connections rise, it's a clear sign of port exhaustion.

jake: Quick sandbox test: adding an extra EIP to a NAT instance increased available SNAT ports linearly. For NAT Gateway in AWS you need multiple NAT Gateways or multiple IPs behind a proxy; AWS NAT Gateway doesn't auto-increase port space per se. Could also run a pool of NAT instances that autoscale based on ActiveConnections.

alex: For the runbook:
- 10:18 — disable prefetch rollouts (priya)
- 10:20 — deploy nginx connection pooler in private subnet and flip egress policy for inference namespace to use it (jake)
- 10:35 — monitor CloudWatch NAT ActiveConnections + pod errors (maria)
- 10:50 — if still high, add NAT gateway in another AZ and update route table (eng-infra ops)

priya: PR created and canary rolled back to 0% now. Patch will land in 5m. :thumbsup:

jake: Deploying nginx pooler as a DaemonSet with a small service and setting `egress` iptables redirect for the namespace now. Config snippet: 
```
proxy_connect_timeout 1s;
proxy_http_version 1.1;
keepalive_timeout 60s;
```

maria: Monitoring — ActiveConnections dropped from 61k -> 18k after the rollback + pooler canary. Error rate from inference pods reduced by ~85%. Looks like the combination worked.

alex: Nice. Next steps:
- Add a short-term ticket to add per-AZ NAT gateways + update runbook (jake)
- Work with infra/infra-networking to evaluate using VPC endpoints for model storage + PrivateLink to telemetry providers (maria)
- Add unit test in prefetch to limit parallel downloads by default (priya)

jake: Filing NAT capacity ticket: INFRA-2482 — add multi-AZ NAT and autoscaling NAT instances as fallback.

priya: Adding the prefetch rate-limit test to the repo now.

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-0318-348 resolved: 1763456920 — mitigation successful, follow-ups assigned.

alex: Thanks all. Please add notes to the eng-infra runbook under "Egress NAT exhaustion" with commands to check CloudWatch and the quick mitigation steps.

maria: Will do. I'll also add a Grafana panel for NAT active ports and per-namespace egress connection counts.

jake: Leaving this thread open for postmortem notes. :eyes:
